public_rationale: The April 2022 Winoground evaluation tested image-caption matching with captions containing the same words in different orders [e1]. All tested models scored below random chance on the group measure, supporting substantial difficulty handling meaning-changing reorderings in contemporary vision-language models [e1]. A November 2022 analysis provides a later qualification: failures also involved combining visual and linguistic information, so they cannot be attributed solely to word-order processing [e2].
limitations: The evidence concerns tested vision-language models, not every contemporary AI approach [e1].
The packet does not quantify performance on the exact cat-and-mat example.
The November analysis falls outside the January 1–June 22, 2022 target period and serves only as methodological context [e2].

evidence.explanation: Winoground requires matching two images to captions containing the same words in different orders. Its poor group scores across contemporary vision-language models support substantial difficulty preserving the changed relationships.

This later analysis finds that visual discrimination and combining visual with linguistic information also affect performance. It limits any inference that word-order processing alone caused the observed failures.
